purpose: Expected calls, tokens, wall-clock and cost for the 480-run Azure matrix. Every figure is extrapolated from the OpenRouter llama cells that DID complete, not from a guess.

measured_basis.note: calls_per_decision exceeds 1 because of economic retries (R, G) and schema repairs. It is measured, not assumed.

llama|G|P_GMV.basis: extrapolated from the 22 completed seeds (7786 calls / 22 = 353.9 calls per run)

llama|G|P_robust.basis: never run on OpenRouter; scaled from llama|R|P_robust by the gemma G/R ratio at P_robust (37567/37177 = 1.0105)

totals.uncertainty: +/- about 3 percent on calls; the two G cells are the extrapolated ones and together are 27 percent of the total

runtime.derivation: 168255 calls at the measured concurrency efficiency of the OpenRouter run (aggregate per-run wall 112356 s at 6 concurrent seeds). Within a round all 4 merchants are called in parallel and the round cannot advance until the slowest returns, which is why the effective speed-up is 1.41x short of the naive 4 x seed_workers.
runtime.recommendation: Start with the default 6. Raise it only if your Azure deployment's tokens-per-minute quota can absorb roughly 1.3 million tokens per minute per 6 workers at 1.9 s latency; otherwise 429s will throttle you back anyway and the retry budget will absorb them.
runtime.interruption: The run is resumable at seed granularity, so it does not need to finish in one sitting. --max-seconds stops cleanly between cells.

cost.warning: These three rows are ILLUSTRATIVE ARITHMETIC, not quoted Azure prices. Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct pricing on Azure AI Foundry varies by region and by whether the deployment is serverless (pay-per-token) or provisioned. Read your own rate card, then set AZURE_PRICE_PER_1M_INPUT and AZURE_PRICE_PER_1M_OUTPUT so that results/summaries/usage_and_cost.json reports the real number instead of null.
cost.dominant_term: Input tokens are 97 percent of the volume. The prompt carries a 21-row payoff table every round, so cost scales with rounds x merchants x runs and is almost independent of how verbose the model is.

what_would_change_these_numbers: A higher schema-repair rate than OpenRouter's (Azure may format differently under response_format=json_object), which would raise calls_per_decision above the measured 1.0634.
Content-filter rejections, which are logged as transport errors and retried, and which do not exist in the OpenRouter baseline at all.
Rate-limit 429s, which cost wall clock but not tokens.
